subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in sender-facing reply for non-allowlisted group senders, and what default, cooldown, raw-ID, and admin-contact semantics should it use?
rationale: The change turns a silent Telegram authorization denial into visible group output and may disclose stable sender IDs or amplify unauthorized traffic, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and documented raw-ID behavior.

options.title: Route Through Operator Audit
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and solve visibility through owner notification or denied-inbound audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and keep logs, docs, and manual Telegram ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for denied-sender onboarding replies with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and documented raw-ID behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined code-history and prior-review signal for the product/security choice, while implementation ownership is shared across recent Telegram contributors.
